reason: None of the cited evidence addresses tribo-corrosion, sliding-induced grain refinement, amorphization, or passive film disruption in HEAs. E1 concerns irradiation resistance, E2 discusses microwave cladding and thermal oxidation, E3 notes that fine grains from processing weaken the passive layer but does not involve wear, and E4 describes boron doping for coatings without mentioning tribological transformations. The key premises thus lack specific prior support from the cited passages.
premises: High strain-rate sliding induces severe grain refinement and dynamic amorphization in the near-surface zone of HEAs.
This nanocrystalline/amorphous layer increases hardness and reduces friction, enhancing wear resistance.
The microstructural transformation disrupts the continuity and protective quality of the passive oxide film.
Disrupted passive film leads to accelerated localized corrosion in corrosive environments.
The overall degradation is governed by a trade-off between improved wear resistance and accelerated corrosion.
